_meta.indication: BYFAVO (remimazolam) for injection is a benzodiazepine indicated for the induction and maintenance of procedural sedation in adults undergoing procedures lasting 30 minutes or less.

pivotal_trials.design: Multi-center, randomized, double-blind, parallel-group, placebo-controlled and active-controlled (midazolam) study; randomization 30:6:10 (remimazolam:placebo:midazolam).
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Difference in sedative success rate between remimazolam and placebo, where success = completion of the procedure, no requirement for rescue sedative medication, and no more than 5 doses of study medication within any 15-minute window.
pivotal_trials.n: Safety population (all treated): Remimazolam 296, Placebo 60, Midazolam 102. The primary efficacy (ITT) analysis used Remimazolam N=298 and Placebo N=60 (see result field).
pivotal_trials.result: Treatment success 272/298 (91.3%) remimazolam vs 1/60 (1.7%) placebo; difference in rates 89.6% (95% CI 85.1, 94.2); P<0.0001.

pivotal_trials.design: Multi-center, randomized, double-blind, parallel-group, placebo-controlled and active-controlled (midazolam) study; randomization 30:6:10 (remimazolam:placebo:midazolam).
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Difference in sedative success rate between remimazolam and placebo (completion of procedure, no rescue sedative required, and no more than 5 doses within any 15-minute window).
pivotal_trials.n: Safety population (all treated): Remimazolam 303, Placebo 59, Midazolam 69. The primary efficacy (ITT) analysis used Remimazolam N=310 and Placebo N=63 (see result field).
pivotal_trials.result: Treatment success 250/310 (80.6%) remimazolam vs 3/63 (4.8%) placebo; difference in rates 75.9% (95% CI 69.0, 82.7); P<0.0001.

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (>10%) are hypotension, hypertension, diastolic hypertension, systolic hypertension, hypoxia, and diastolic hypotension. In the colonoscopy study, hypotension occurred in 39% and hypertension in 20% of BYFAVO patients. Clinically notable hypoxia, bradycardia, and hypotension were observed in Phase 3 studies.
target_moa: BYFAVO is a benzodiazepine that binds to brain benzodiazepine sites (GABAA receptors); it is an ester-based drug hydrolyzed by carboxylesterase-1 (CES-1) to the inactive metabolite CNS7054, which has a 300 times lower affinity for the receptor.

boxed_warning.content: Boxed warning for personnel and equipment for monitoring and resuscitation, and risks from concomitant use with opioid analgesics and other sedative-hypnotics. Only trained personnel should administer BYFAVO; concomitant use of benzodiazepines and opioid analgesics may result in profound sedation, respiratory depression, coma, and death.

rems.type: A REMS is not indicated at this time.

advisory_committee.vote: An advisory committee meeting was not convened for this application.

summary.text: BYFAVO was approved as a 505(b)(2) NDA under standard review, with no accelerated approval, breakthrough, fast track, orphan, or priority-review designations. Approval was contingent on DEA scheduling; remimazolam is a Schedule IV controlled substance.
